findings.evidence: Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears.
findings.fix: Split the manager's countersigning instruction into its own sentence or subsection addressed explicitly to the manager, and keep the you address in this paragraph limited to the employee's own actions.
findings.violation: The paragraph addresses the employee reader directly as you in the first and third sentences, then inserts an unsigned imperative, Countersign the employee request, that only makes sense as an instruction to the manager, with no separation or signal marking the audience change, so a reader cannot tell whether that sentence is theirs to act on.

findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. [...] the policy applies to one device per category per employee.
findings.fix: Pick one term for the purchased equipment, for example equipment item, and use it in every section instead of stipend item, reimbursable item, and device.

findings.violation: The document uses stipend item, reimbursable item, and device interchangeably for what appears to be the same purchased equipment, with no defined-terms section or stated equivalence, so a reader cannot tell whether the three terms name the same thing or three different things.

findings.evidence: Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.

findings.evidence: A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.

findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review.
findings.fix: Keep one running subject across the paragraph, or add an explicit link, for example: Finance then reconciles that item, so the reader can track who is acting at each step.
findings.violation: Each of the paragraph's three sentences introduces a new subject, you, then Finance, then Payroll, with no sentence signalling how the new actor connects to the one before it, so the reader has to re-orient at every sentence boundary instead of following one running topic.

findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing.

findings.violation: 3 comma-set-off clause(s) totalling 14 words intervene between the sentence's apparent subject and its verb.

findings.evidence: An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The...

findings.violation: The paragraph opens with none of the fixed transition words, so the reader is not told how it relates to the paragraph before it.
